description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: backlog list --track filter to show only core or feature items
items.intent: Running backlog list --track core shows only core-track items, and --track feature shows only feature-track items. Without a track filter, users cannot isolate core work from feature work in one command.
steps: In .aishore/lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, add val:filter_track:--track to the parse_opts call in cmd_backlog_list
Validate filter_track after parsing: if set, must be core or feature; call log_error and return 1 on invalid value
When filter_track is set, append a jq filter segment: select((.track // "feature") == "$filter_track") to the existing jq_filter pipeline
In .aishore/lib/cmd-help.sh, add --track <t> entry under backlog list options in _help_backlog(), aligned with existing filter flags
items.lastFailReason: Baseline validation failed before developer ran
items.groomingNotes: Track filter missing from backlog list despite TRACK column being shown. Pattern matches --type/--priority/--status. 4-line implementation.

items.title: status shows core not-configured hint when CORE_CMD is absent
items.intent: When no CORE_CMD is configured, aishore status must print a visible hint pointing to scaffold. Silent omission leaves users unaware that the working core gate is inactive and they do not know to run scaffold.
steps: In .aishore/lib/cmd-status.sh, in _status_output(), locate the if [[ -n "$CORE_CMD" ]] block that shows core health
Add an else branch: print a line such as Core: not configured — run scaffold to establish CORE_CMD, using log_info or log_warning styling
Place the hint in the same visual section as core health (after the ready summary), so it is visible without scrolling

acceptanceCriteria.text: status shows not-configured hint when CORE_CMD is empty

items.lastFailReason: Baseline validation failed before developer ran
items.groomingNotes: UX gap: status silently omits core section when CORE_CMD is absent. Adding else branch with scaffold hint.

items.title: backlog show displays sprint history from archive for the item
items.intent: When an item has sprint runs in archive/sprints.jsonl, backlog show must display a Sprint history section listing each run: date, status, and attempts. Without this, sprint history is invisible — users must manually grep the archive file.
steps: In cmd_backlog_show in .aishore/lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, after the existing jq output block, look up the item ID in $ARCHIVE_DIR/sprints.jsonl
Use jq to select all entries where .itemId == the queried ID, sorted by .date ascending, limited to 10 most recent
If matching entries exist, print a Sprint history: header followed by each entry formatted as: date  status  (attempts: N)
If no archive entries exist for the item, omit the section entirely — do not print an empty header

acceptanceCriteria.text: show exits 0 for item with no archive entries
acceptanceCriteria.verify: id=$(.aishore/aishore backlog add --json "{\"title\":\"tmp-show-test\",\"intent\":\"temp item to verify backlog show works without archive data\"}" 2>&1 | grep -o "FEAT-[0-9]*") && .aishore/aishore backlog show "$id" && .aishore/aishore backlog rm "$id" --force

acceptanceCriteria.text: Sprint history section appears for item with archive entry

items.title: backlog list summary line includes ready count
items.intent: The final summary line of backlog list must show both total and ready counts, e.g. N item(s), M ready. Currently it shows only N item(s), requiring a separate status run to see how many items are sprint-ready.
steps: In cmd_backlog_list in .aishore/lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, add a ready_count=0 variable before the output loop
Inside the while-read loop, increment ready_count when the ready column value equals yes
Change the final printf at the end of the function from printf %s item(s) to printf %s item(s), %s ready using ready_count as the second argument

items.title: status shows core/feature split for ready items when CORE_CMD is configured
items.intent: When CORE_CMD is configured and core is healthy, aishore status must show how many ready items are core-track vs feature-track. Without this split, users cannot tell if the ready buffer contains core work or only feature work.

Print the split only when CORE_CMD is set: echo indented core: N ready, feature: M ready
Reuse the same jq pattern already present in the CORE_CMD failing branch (around line 78-87 of cmd-status.sh) for consistency

items.title: backlog show falls back to archive for done/cleaned items
items.intent: backlog show <ID> must succeed for any item aishore has ever tracked — active or archived. Running backlog show on a done item that was cleaned must display the item with an [archived] label rather than failing with item not found.
items.description: dal_find_item searches only the active BACKLOG_DIR files. Once aishore clean archives completed items, backlog show <ID> returns an error. Fix: after find_item fails in cmd_backlog_show, search archive/backlog_done.json and archive/bugs_done.json, display with an archived label, exit 0.
steps: In cmd_backlog_show in lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, after find_item fails, search ARCHIVE_DIR/backlog_done.json and ARCHIVE_DIR/bugs_done.json for the item ID
Archive files store items as a JSON array at the top level. Use: jq -e --arg id ID .[] | select(.id == $id) on each archive file
If found in archive, print an [archived] header line then display the item with the existing jq display block
Return 0 so callers do not treat archived item display as a failure
Only error when the item is not found in any file — active backlog or archive

acceptanceCriteria.text: backlog show on an archived done item displays the item with archived label
backlog show on archived item exits 0
backlog show on an unknown ID still exits non-zero

items.title: backlog list --track filter for core or feature track
items.intent: backlog list --track core must show only core-track items and backlog list --track feature must show only feature items. Invalid values must be rejected with an error. This lets users review the core pipeline independently from features before starting a session.
items.description: cmd_backlog_list has no --track filter. With core/feature tracks gating sprint picks, users need to quickly audit the core pipeline separately. The fix is a --track flag in parse_opts that narrows the jq filter.
steps: Add filter_track local variable and bool:filter_track or val:filter_track:--track to parse_opts in cmd_backlog_list in lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh
Validate the value is core or feature; reject anything else with a clear error message
When filter_track is set, append select(.track // "feature" == $track) to jq_filter and pass the value as --arg track to the jq call

acceptanceCriteria.text: backlog list --track invalid exits non-zero with an error message
backlog list --track core header line is present in output

items.title: run batch session prints sprint summary table at end
items.intent: After any auto-mode run session completes, a sprint summary must print — one row per item attempted showing ID, pass/fail, and attempts — followed by totals and elapsed time. The operator must not have to scroll the full log to know the session outcome.
items.description: cmd_run exits after run_sprint_loop without printing a summary. In auto mode (run done / run p0 / run p1), the operator has no quick recap. The fix is to print a summary table at the end of cmd_run when auto_mode is true, using the sprint_items, COMPLETED_IDS, and FAILED_IDS state already tracked in the loop.
steps: After run_sprint_loop returns in cmd_run (aishore main script, cmd_run function), check if auto_mode is true
Print a Sprint Session Summary header using log_header
Print a table: ITEM | STATUS | ATTEMPTS for each item in sprint_items[], looking up pass/fail from COMPLETED_IDS and FAILED_IDS associative arrays
Print totals line: X complete, Y failed, Z skipped
Print elapsed time from batch_start to now in minutes

acceptanceCriteria.text: run done with no items drains cleanly and exits 0
Sprint Session Summary header appears in auto-mode output
